query_text: Need a web app where illustrators and clients can team up on commissions — I want a board where you can post a brief, browse artist styles, leave feedback on sketches, and track where a project is in the process, all in one place for desktop browsers.

A cold outreach email sequence builder for freelancers — a web app where I can write a series of follow-up emails, set a rough schedule for when each one goes out, and keep track of which potential clients I've already contacted, so I stop losing leads because I forgot to follow up.

A retainer tracker tool for freelancers, browser-based, where I can log each monthly client retainer, list out exactly what deliverables are included, check things off as I finish them, and quickly see if I'm about to go over scope before it becomes a problem.

Create a web app calculator for freelancers that shows how profitable each project actually is — I plug in what I charged, how many hours I spent, and any costs I had, and it tells me my real hourly rate and margin so I can finally figure out which clients are actually worth taking on.

Need a skills tracker tool for freelancers that runs in the browser, where I can list everything I currently know how to do, rate myself on each skill, and then see a clear gap analysis showing what I should learn next to get better-paying work in my field.

A testimonial request manager for freelancers — a web app where I can see a list of past clients, send them a quick message asking for a review or reference, and keep track of who's responded and who I'm still waiting on, so I stop letting that stuff fall through the cracks.

Need a certification tracker app for freelancers, accessible from a desktop browser, where I can list all my licenses and professional certs, set expiration dates, and get reminded before they run out so I never accidentally let something lapse.

Need a web app analyzer tool that helps me figure out whether a freelance niche is worth going after — I want to enter a skill or service area and see roughly how much demand there is, who's already competing in that space, and whether it makes sense for me to focus there.

A dental clinic website where visitors can meet the whole team with photos and short bios, and also take a quick tour of the facility — rooms, equipment, that sort of thing — so new patients feel comfortable before they even book an appointment, all viewable on a desktop browser.

Need a website for an artisan cheese and charcuterie shop that shows off the full product range — each item with a photo, a short description of where it's from, and maybe tasting notes — so customers browsing on desktop can actually get excited about what to order.

Need a portfolio website for a residential interior design studio that showcases finished projects — each project gets its own space with before-and-after photos, a brief description of what was done, and maybe the style or room type — so potential clients browsing on desktop can get a real feel for the work.

A neighborhood gym showcase website for desktop browsers where people can see all the equipment and training floor areas — photos of the machines, the free weights section, the cardio area — along with a short description of each so folks checking it out online know exactly what they're getting before they visit.

Need a website for a local catering company that shows off their signature dishes with appetizing photos and descriptions, plus a gallery of past events they've done — weddings, corporate lunches, parties — so potential clients on desktop can browse and get inspired before reaching out.

Need a website for a pottery studio that shows off handmade ceramics from classes and the studio itself — photos of finished pieces organized by type like mugs, bowls, vases — and a gallery of what happens during classes, so people browsing on desktop can see the work and get a feel for the vibe before signing up.

Need a website for a therapeutic massage center that lists all the services with descriptions and pricing, plus profiles of each therapist with their specialties and a short bio, so clients can browse on desktop and actually pick the right person and treatment before they book.

Build a spa education web app with a calm, organic feel — like flipping through a beautiful wellness journal — where each treatment has its own space explaining the key ingredients, where they come from, and what they do for your skin or body, with soft imagery and a clean layout that feels luxurious on desktop.

Need a web app blog hub for a small plumbing business — a warm, approachable site where homeowners can browse practical how-to articles about maintaining their pipes, fixing small leaks, and preventing common problems, with a cozy layout that feels like trusted advice from a neighbor rather than a cold manual.

Need a web app blog for a local plant nursery that feels like walking through a lush garden — seasonal care guides and planting tips organized by time of year, with beautiful plant photography and a calm earthy aesthetic, so readers on desktop feel like they're getting advice from someone who really loves plants.

A web app diary for an independent watch repair shop — a beautifully crafted restoration journal where each entry shows a watch that came in for repair, the story behind it, close-up photos of the movement, and what the craftsman did to bring it back to life, with a timeless aesthetic that feels right at home on desktop.

Need a web app blog for a neighborhood laundry shop with a clean, satisfying aesthetic — articles and tips about how to care for different fabrics, treat stubborn stains, and keep clothes looking fresh, laid out in a way that feels helpful and easy to read on desktop, like a trusted guide from someone who really knows their stuff.

Make a music school blog web app for desktop browsers where each post captures the warmth of a student recital — photos from recent performances, little stories about how students have grown, and practical practice tips for different instruments, all with a cozy and encouraging vibe that makes parents and students feel seen.

An event rental company lookbook website where the whole thing feels like a beautifully styled magazine spread — each page shows a different styled shoot, with gorgeous photos of tablescapes, lighting setups, and decor arrangements, grouped by theme or season, so potential clients browsing on desktop can dream up their own event and see exactly what's possible.

Need a web app for a local grocery store that handles weekend flash deals — customers on desktop can pull it up and immediately see what's on sale this weekend, with the item, original price, deal price, and how long the deal lasts, so the store doesn't have to keep texting people or printing flyers every week.

Make a website for a language school where people can sign up for a free trial lesson — the site should explain what languages are available, let visitors pick a time slot, and fill in their name and contact info, all in a browser-based form that actually works without someone having to call in or send an email.

Need a simple web app promo site for a car wash that wants to sell monthly subscription plans — people on desktop can see the different membership tiers, what each one includes, the price, and sign up right there, so the business doesn't have to explain the same thing over and over at the counter.
